![Bringing Traditional Drinks of Thailand to Nashua - The Giant ...](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/07261836-1672-0139-0000-fa80e13a58e1:4)
Thai non-alcoholic drinks range from globally celebrated sweet creamy teas to refreshing herbal infusions. The most iconic is **Cha Yen** (Thai Iced Tea), an amber blend of strong black tea, spices (star anise, crushed cardamom), sugar, and condensed milk.[](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/DJQF3MpKhOc) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/DJQF3MpKhOc)[[2]](https://www.facebook.com/ThaiPBSWorld/videos/thailands-orange-iconic-cha-yen-thai-tea-has-been-named-the-9th-best-non-alcohol/1528597198972265/)[[3]](https://thesobercurator.com/5-thai-herbal-drinks-alcohol-free-bar-crawl/)[[4]](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/3248879/thai-iced-tea-ranked-ninth-among-worlds-best-nonalcoholic-drinks)

Discover the diverse range of Thai non-alcoholic beverages, categorized by style:

1. Iconic & Creamy Drinks

- **Cha Yen (Thai Iced Tea):** The most famous Thai drink globally. Brewed with strongly spiced Ceylon or Assam black tea, sweetened with condensed milk, and topped with evaporated milk for a rich, layered look.[](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/DJQF3MpKhOc) [[1]](https://www.facebook.com/AmazingThailand/videos/refreshments-thai-stylewhen-it-comes-to-beverages-thai-style-drinks-are-equally-/512311552845976/)[[2]](https://guide.michelin.com/th/en/article/features/iconic-dishes-thai-milk-tea-explained)[[3]](https://mykeythai.com/journal/guides/thai-tea-chatramue-guide)
- **Nom Yen (Pink Milk):** A sweet, caffeine-free favorite made by mixing Sala syrup (a sweet, floral fruit syrup from the salacca fruit) with milk or condensed milk.
- **Oliang (Thai Iced Coffee):** A strong, dark iced coffee traditionally brewed from a blend of coffee beans, roasted corn, soybeans, and sesame seeds, sweetened and served over ice.[[1]](https://www.thai-food-online.co.uk/blogs/thai-food-online-blog/thai-iced-drink-recipes-for-summer)[[2]](https://www.mamanoicookingschool.com/blog/thai-traditional-foods/)[[3]](https://www.latimes.com/recipe/longan-juice)[[4]](https://www.homegrounds.co/thai-iced-coffee-recipe/)

2. Traditional Herbal Teas

- **Nam Matoom:** A traditional herbal tea made from dried bael fruit. It is earthy, sweet, and typically consumed to aid digestion.
- **Roselle Juice:** A tart, ruby-red drink made by steeping dried hibiscus flowers. Served very sweet over ice, it is Thailand's refreshing answer to the Western zinger tea.
- **Chrysanthemum Tea:** A bright, golden beverage with a subtle floral aroma that is prized for its cooling properties.

3. Fruity & Refreshing Beverages

- **Nam Manao:** The Thai version of lemonade, made with freshly squeezed lime juice, water, and simple syrup. You can easily elevate this by adding muddled Thai basil or lemongrass.[](https://mindfulmocktail.com/virgin-mai-tai-mocktail/) [[1]](https://mindfulmocktail.com/virgin-mai-tai-mocktail/)[[2]](https://whitecoconutthai.com/must-try-authentic-drinks-of-thailand-burlington-mall-white-coconut/)[[3]](https://steemit.com/cookwithus/@loveself/cookwithus-5-tom-yum-mocktail)
- **Mogu Mogu:** A popular commercial line of fruit juice drinks (such as lychee or mango) from Thailand that uniquely includes *nata de coco* (chewy coconut jelly).[[1]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:11179333417994305337&ibp=oshop)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:736800114003925803,catalogid:16531774859018392846,gpcid:14640191894886016944,mid:576462800795549161&ibp=oshop)[[3]](https://www.ubereats.com/gb/store/thai2go/AJ4o-QpmT7CbG8Pt8EE4DQ)[[4]](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Lychee-Flavoured-Drink-320ml-Vegan/dp/B0DZPCHJGF)[[5]](https://www.killercandy.co.uk/products/mogu-mogu-apple-juice-drink)

4. Modern Bottled Options

- **Singha Lemon Soda:** A popular canned refreshment in Thailand that is zero-sugar, zero-calorie, and known for its crisp, "grease-cutting" fizz.[[1]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:16776406182352236273,catalogid:3386714749516276844,gpcid:2272078081752942603,mid:576462433654067708&ibp=oshop)[[2]](https://www.joybuy.co.uk/blog/thai-drinks-best-uk-guide/7M52Dtpf)[[3]](https://www.mamanoicookingschool.com/blog/thai-drinks/)[[4]](https://www.goldenacrewines.co.uk/product/singha-lemon-soda-zero-sugar-300ml/)
- **Oishi Green Tea:** Ubiquitous in Thai convenience stores, these bottled green teas come in sweet, honey, or Genmai (roasted rice) flavors.

Explore more authentic Thai tea varieties or check out regional recipes to make at home on sites like TasteAtlas or food blogs like The Spruce Eats.
